prompt:
A simulated brick world had this hidden rule:
In this world each placement lands at the left-right mirror of the chosen anchor: a brick dx cells wide chosen at column x lands at column 8 - dx - x, in the same row. The valid-action mask is in the agent's own action terms. The designs and scoring are as described.

Below is what an AI scientist wrote during a search in that world: its analysis at every round, in order, and the
name and hypothesis of the trial it ended with. Does the text, anywhere, state the rule?
- "yes": it states the rule's substance (what is changed and how).
- "partly": it identifies the right kind of change but not its specifics.
- "no": anything else.

## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
The untrained trace shows that the world mirrors the column index of every action. A 1x1 at col 2 fills col 5, and a 1x2 at col 6 fills cols 0-1, so the filled cells start at column X-dx-x. Rows are not changed. The starting network scores each anchor from local conv features at that same anchor, so it cannot link an action to the cells it actually fills. Random placements then earn negative reward, and PPO settles on DONE at the first step (100% of dev episodes; training episode length falls to 1.0). Restoring the mapping should be the main lever. Flipping the feature map along x before the footprint-pooling head lines each anchor up with exactly the cells it fills, for every footprint width. I test that flip directly, the flip with a recipe change against the DONE collapse, and a general learned axis-mixing layer that could learn any permutation without hard-coding the mirror.

### Round 2
In this world the x axis is mirrored: action column x fills the columns from X-dx-x to X-1-x, while rows are not mirrored. Flipping the feature map along x before the footprint head took dev success from 0 to 0.745 (r1c1). Adding ppo_epochs 3 and ent_coef 0.03 raised it to 0.793 (r1c2). That gap is inside the seed noise, since r1c2's two seeds alone were 0.85 and 0.73. Learned mixing of row and column positions (r1c3) did not learn the flip within the budget and scored 0.045. In both flip runs, training success was still climbing steeply at the end of training (0.51 to 0.74 over the last quarter), so the agent is short of samples. The dev builds already match most target cells (IoU 0.98), so the remaining failures are probably about placement order: overhangs, and knowing which cells are still to be filled. Each next trial makes one change to r1c2: fewer epochs for more samples, a higher discount so the end-of-episode success bonus reaches early steps, or global context in the placement head.

### Round 3
Flipping the feature map along x before the placement head is what makes learning work: it scored 0.75 to 0.90, against 0.00 for the starting architecture. Learning that remapping with mixing matrices failed (0.04). The clearest result is the sample count. ppo_epochs 3 gave about 160k steps and scored 0.79; ppo_epochs 2 gave about 229k steps and scored 0.90, with training success still rising at the end. That points to a sample limit, so ppo_epochs 1 (about 426k steps) is the obvious next test. Gamma 0.99 (0.82) and global context in the head (0.78) are within the roughly 6 to 12 point seed spread of their baseline (0.79), so neither clearly helped. Dev IoU is about 0.98 with about 0.4 extra cells per episode, so the remaining failures are probably a few wrong placements (order or overhang errors). Trials take about 70 seconds against the 900-second limit, so time is not a constraint.

### Round 4
Two changes account for almost all of the progress. The x-flip before the head fixed the mirrored action mapping (0 to 0.75). Fewer PPO epochs, which buys more samples, raised success further: 3 epochs gave 0.79, 2 gave 0.90, 1 gave 0.92, and 1 epoch with 64 minibatches gave 0.96 (best, seeds 0.97 and 0.95). Several ideas did not help: learned axis mixing (0.04), global context added to the head (0.78), the dilated conv (0.72) and gamma 0.99 (0.82, within noise of its comparison). Seed noise is about 2 to 6 points. r3c2's training success stops rising at about 0.90 by 75% of training with the entropy coefficient at 0.03. That suggests more learning per sample (higher learning rate) or less exploration noise. The remaining errors are a few cells placed outside the target, which suggests the head sometimes misjudges landing layers. Raw per-column layer features passed straight to the head may fix that.

## Trial it ended with
name: flip, 1 epoch, 64 minibatches
hypothesis: Change: ppo_epochs 1 as in the first candidate, plus n_minibatches 64 (64 samples per minibatch). This keeps about 426k steps and doubles the gradient steps per sample.
